teams.heading: Jake White criticises Fiji's tap-penalty call in 43-15 Dublin defeat
teams.body: Jake White was frustrated that Fiji chose a tap penalty over a scrum when the game was in the balance in the second half of Saturday's 43-15 defeat in Dublin. The former South Africa coach, appointed last month, said the Springboks would have kept taking scrums to bait Ireland into a yellow card. White's verdict was that Fiji "did Ireland a favour", because Ireland know they would be up against it playing like that against South Africa.

lead.why: It is a new post-match reaction from Fiji's own coach, which gives the reader a Fiji-side angle on the Ireland defeat without repeating the result.

teams.heading: Matt Dawson urges England to embrace favourites tag against All Blacks
teams.body: Fresh from a 78-15 win over Japan at Twickenham, Matt Dawson's BBC column argues England should lean into the role. "I would love to see the England players absolutely bombarded with the favourites tag before their meeting with New Zealand," he writes, and says he genuinely believes they are favourites. Dawson also credits Wales' 35-28 win over the All Blacks in Cardiff with giving him real faith in this England side.

lead.why: The strongest new England-focused item; the Joseph and Kay pieces rehash already-run stories or centre on Wales.

teams.heading: Matthieu Jalibert recalled to France squad for Argentina Test; Hugo Avogadro named
teams.body: Jalibert replaces Louis Le Brun in the 42-man group named for Saturday's Test, ending a spell out since a right quadriceps tear on 20 September that was set back by a relapse in mid-October. The other main options, Romain Ntamack, Thomas Ramos and Antoine Hastoy, are all injured. Anthony Jelonch, back from a concussion sustained at Pau, and Nicolas Depoortere also return, while Bordeaux Bègles winger Hugo Avogadro earns his first senior call-up. Julien Marchand is not on the list.

lead.why: A fresh France selection event with Jalibert's return and Avogadro's first senior call-up, ahead of the Argentina Test.

teams.heading: Jamie Osborne and James McNabney both out of Springboks test, Farrell confirms
teams.body: Two of Ireland's options for the Springboks test went off injured in the 43-15 win over Fiji, and Andy Farrell's update leaves both short of contention. Outside centre Jamie Osborne was replaced in the fourth minute with what looks like a pec problem, while James McNabney's brief debut ended with a head injury and a 12-day return-to-play protocol. Farrell said McNabney was "in our thoughts 100%" for next week. Tighthead Sam Illo is a major doubt after entering head injury assessment.

lead.why: Farrell's post-match update brings new injury news that rules two backs out of the Springboks test.

teams.heading: Foreign press says Italy dominated Argentina but wasted chances in Genoa defeat
teams.body: Italy's 19-14 defeat to Argentina in Genoa on Saturday is being read abroad as a match the Azzurri controlled for long spells before wasting their chances. RugbyPass said Quesada's side looked transformed from the team beaten 66-7 by South Africa a week earlier, but failed to make its spell of dominance count. Planetrugby pinpointed Italy's lineout throw, which worked to international standard only rarely, as one of the main reasons they could not capitalise on pressure.

lead.why: The only NEW item about Italy's own story: how foreign outlets read the Argentina defeat, rather than a repeat of the match report or a rival's news.

teams.heading: Russell penalty ends Wallabies' late rally as Scotland edge Australia 15-12
teams.body: Finn Russell's penalty in the 74th minute put Scotland two scores clear at Murrayfield, and the Dark Blues held firm after Max Jorgensen's 79th-minute try, with Darcy Graham and Blair Kinghorn frustrating a last-ditch Australia attack. Scotland had led 12-5 at half-time on tries from Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey, and the result lifts them above Wales into fourth in the Northern Hemisphere table. Captain Sione Tuipulotu was ruled out with a knee injury before kick-off.

lead.why: It is a new report of Scotland's 15-12 win over Australia, with a clear decisive moment (Russell's late penalty) and a Scotland-side angle, and it outranks the background items.

teams.heading: Alfie Prygodzicz inspires Wales U19s to 34-31 comeback win over France
teams.body: Wales U19s beat France U19s 34-31 at St Helen's on Saturday, with Cardiff back-row Alfie Prygodzicz leading the side from the front. France led 17-5 at half-time, but Wales scored 24 unanswered points after the restart, and Prygodzicz crossed twice in quick succession to put his side in command. It was Wales' first win over France at any age-grade level for six years, and the young side had watched the senior team beat the All Blacks in their hotel beforehand.

lead.why: A fresh Wales pathway result with a clear Welsh angle, and the other new items are either retellings of the All Blacks win or other teams' stories.

teams.heading: Pumas' messy 19-14 Genoa win over Italy gets lukewarm foreign reviews
teams.body: Argentina's 19-14 win over Italy in Genoa on Saturday was read abroad as hard-earned rather than convincing. RugbyPass called the game disordered and said Argentina got the win in the end. L'Équipe described it as a small victory after a sad match, while Franceinfo noted the Pumas struggled until the final whistle, with France next on the agenda.

lead.why: A new item on how the European press judged Argentina's narrow win in Genoa, which is a fresh angle on an already-reported result.

teams.heading: Max Jorgensen's late try falls short as Wallabies lose 15-12 at Murrayfield
teams.body: The Wallabies were beaten 15-12 at Murrayfield on Sunday, their fourth straight Test defeat, despite a late rally. Harry Potter's try had levelled the scores after Matt Fagerson opened for Scotland, but Jack Dempsey's score before half-time left Australia 5-12 down at the break. Finn Russell's penalty in the 74th minute put Scotland two scores clear before Jorgensen crossed late. Defensively the Wallabies were markedly better, with Fraser McReight making 26 tackles without a miss.

lead.why: It is the fresh match-result report on Australia's Sunday defeat, and the most talked-about event in today's coverage.

teams.heading: Kriel extends Yokohama Canon Eagles stay to 2028 as Springboks head home
teams.body: Jesse Kriel will not be joining the Springbok exodus from Japan, having signed a further two years at Yokohama Canon Eagles, until June 2028. The centre has been at the club since 2020. Faf de Klerk, Cheslin Kolbe, Malcolm Marx, Kwagga Smith and Manie Libbok have all signed in South Africa, with Pieter-Steph du Toit and Damian de Allende reportedly heading home. Kriel, who has no family to consider, said: "I'm also really enjoying my rugby in Japan."

lead.why: The only new item with a Japan angle; the Wales piece is another team's story, and the Japan previews and profiles concern the match already played.

teams.heading: Mark Watson calls All Blacks' Wales defeat 'a death in the family'
teams.body: Radio host Mark Watson said he felt 'embarrassed' and 'humiliated' after the All Blacks' 35-28 loss to Wales in Cardiff, which felt 'a little bit like a death in the family'. He called it possibly the worst performance in All Black history, while conceding Wales deserved the win. Watson set it apart from recent heavy defeats to South Africa and in Baltimore, which he argued came at the hands of world champions. Tries from Cortez Ratima, Wallace Sititi, Fehi Fineanganofo and Peter Lakai were not enough.

lead.why: A fresh, New Zealand-focused post-match verdict from a well-known local broadcaster, naming the 35-28 Cardiff defeat and the players singled out.

teams.heading: Kitshoff expects Springboks to respond angrily to Paris defeat in Dublin
teams.body: Friday's 21-19 loss to France in Paris has left the world champions with plenty to fix, and Steven Kitshoff expects a furious response in Dublin. On the For the Love of Rugby podcast, he said "I don’t think it’s going to be an easy week" and pointed to "a massive uproar within the Springbok camp". His plan for the Boks is a big set-piece battle first, taking away Ireland's legs, then shutting down their structured play. South Africa must beat Ireland and hope England do them a favour.

lead.why: A fresh player reaction to the Paris defeat that sets up the Ireland test, and it is the strongest new South Africa item on offer.
